ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are four points on the circle $\odot O$. $AB=AC$, $AD$ intersects $BC$ at point $E$, $AE=4$, and $ED=6$. What is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \text{Since } AB=AC, \]
\[ \therefore \angle ABE=\angle ACE, \]
\[ \text{Since } \angle ACE=\angle ADB, \]
\[ \therefore \angle ABE=\angle ADB, \]
\[ \text{Since } \angle BAE=\angle DAB, \]
\[ \therefore \triangle ABE\sim \triangle ADB, \]
\[ \therefore \frac{AB}{AD}=\frac{AE}{AB}, \]
\[ \text{Thus, } AB^2=AD\cdot AE, \]
\[ \text{Since } AE=4, ED=6, \]
\[ \therefore AD=10, \]
\[ \therefore AB=\sqrt{AD\cdot AE}=\sqrt{10\times 4}=2\sqrt{10}, \]
\[ \therefore AC=AB=2\sqrt{10}, \]
\[ \text{Hence, the answer is: } AC=\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}. \]

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are four points on the circle $\odot O$. $AB=AC$, $AD$ intersects $BC$ at point $E$, $AE=4$, and $ED=6$. What is the length of $AC$?
raw_record.answer:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \text{Since } AB=AC, \]
\[ \therefore \angle ABE=\angle ACE, \]
\[ \text{Since } \angle ACE=\angle ADB, \]
\[ \therefore \angle ABE=\angle ADB, \]
\[ \text{Since } \angle BAE=\angle DAB, \]
\[ \therefore \triangle ABE\sim \triangle ADB, \]
\[ \therefore \frac{AB}{AD}=\frac{AE}{AB}, \]
\[ \text{Thus, } AB^2=AD\cdot AE, \]
\[ \text{Since } AE=4, ED=6, \]
\[ \therefore AD=10, \]
\[ \therefore AB=\sqrt{AD\cdot AE}=\sqrt{10\times 4}=2\sqrt{10}, \]
\[ \therefore AC=AB=2\sqrt{10}, \]
\[ \text{Hence, the answer is: } AC=\boxed{2\sqrt{10}}. \]
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a circle, A is above the circle, B is on the left-side circumference, C is on the right-side circumference, D is on the lower-right circumference; line segment AD and line segment BC intersect at point E inside the circle, and E lies on AD and also lies on BC; BD is also drawn in the figure, so triangles ABE and ADB can be compared. The problem gives AB=AC, AE=4, ED=6.

Reasoning: Because E is on BC, ∠ABE=∠ABC, ∠ACE=∠ACB. Also because AB=AC, triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, that is, ∠ABC=∠ACB, therefore ∠ABE=∠ACE. Since A, B, C, D are concyclic, ∠ACE and ∠ADB both subtend the same arc AB, so ∠ACE=∠ADB, hence ∠ABE=∠ADB. Also because E is on AD, ∠BAE=∠DAB. Thus triangle ABE and triangle ADB are similar. From the corresponding side relationship of similarity, AB/AD = AE/AB, therefore AB²=AD·AE. It is known that AE=4, ED=6, so AD=AE+ED=10. Thus AB²=10×4=40, AB=2√10. Also AB=AC, so AC=2√10.
